headline: Signed two Chapter Land Liens for 21 Colonial Drive and 112 Town Farm Road, plus three exemption denial notices.
summary: The meeting also accepted the minutes of September 15 and discussed changes to the Senior Work off Policy, with a final review set for the next meeting. The Principal Assessor contacted Mass Electric about a court case and has not yet received its opinion of value. The group then met in executive session to review abatement and exemption applications, which state law limits to assessors and certain others.
decisions: Accepted the September 15, 2026 open and executive session minutes unanimously.
Signed two Chapter Land Liens, for 21 Colonial Drive and 112 Town Farm Road.
Signed three property tax exemption denial notices (State Tax Form 135).

plain_text:
TOWN OF SUTTON
BOARD OF ASSESSORS
 4 UXBRIDGE ROAD
SUTTON, MA  01590-1702
  508-865-8722
Meeting Minutes – September 22, 2026
Present: Robert Nunnemacher, Chairman
 Tracey Tardy, Principal Assessor
 Matthew Read, Assessor
Meeting called to order at 5:07 p.m.
1.         The Board voted unanimously to accept the open session meeting minutes and executive session
            meeting minutes of September 15, 2026
2.         Old & New Business
The Board discussed implementing a few changes to the Senior Work off Policy – the Board will update the
draft policy and review the final changes next meeting
The Principal Assessor reached out to Mass Electric regarding the court case as we are still waiting their
opinion of value – no answer yet
3.         Decisions & Actions Taken
The Board signed two (2) Chapter Land Liens:
21 Colonial Drive
112 Town Farm Road
The Board signed three (3) State Tax Form 135 – Property Tax Exemption Denial Notices
4. Adjourned Open Session @ 5:30 to enter into Executive Session regarding
            Abatements/Exemptions
The Board entered into executive session to review abatement and/or exemption applications pursuant
to Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 59, Section 60, and Chapter 30A, Section 21, Item number 7. We are 
meeting in executive session to comply with Chapter 59, Section 60, which limits inspection of Chapter 59 
abatement and exemption applications to assessors and the deputies, clerks and assistants of the assessors, and 
certain other parties listed in the law. Chapter 30A, Section 21, Item number 7 permits public bodies to meet in 
executive session for the purpose of complying with general laws. 
The Board of Assessors adjourned its open meeting at or about 5:30 p.m. 
Respectfully Submitted,
Linda Hicks, Assistant Assessor
